data.name: Herat
data.shortDescription: Herat is a historic western city and a major Timurid cultural centre.

profile.culture: Persian/Dari poetry, miniature and traditional arts.
profile.economy: Herat economy: agriculture (grapes, saffron), trade with Iran, growing industrial parks and manufacturing.
profile.tourism: Herat Citadel, Friday Mosque, Musalla Minarets, Khwaja Abdullah Ansari Shrine.
profile.overview: Historic western city; major Silk Road and Timurid cultural centre with Persianate heritage.
profile.unescoSites: Herat historic city on UNESCO Tentative List
profile.transportation: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari International Airport; buses/minibuses/taxis; Herat–Kandahar Highway.
profile.majorIndustries: agro-processing, textiles, saffron production, light manufacturing
profile.traditionalFood: Herati rice dishes, mantu, ashak, qorma
profile.shortDescription: Herat is a historic western city and a major Timurid cultural centre.

data.name: Kabul
data.shortDescription: Kabul is the national capital and largest urban centre of Afghanistan.

profile.culture: Dari/Pashto poetry, music, handicrafts, hospitality and traditional dress.
profile.economy: Kabul is the economic centre of Afghanistan: agriculture, trade, industrial parks, manufacturing, retail, hotels and real estate.
profile.tourism: Bagh-e Babur, Darul Aman Palace, Kabul Citadel/Bala Hissar, National Museum, Qargha Reservoir, Paghman.
profile.overview: National capital and largest city; ancient settlement and long-standing political centre.
profile.geography: Kabul River; cold semi-arid/continental climate; located in a mountain valley.
profile.entertainment: Afghan films/documentaries and television; football, cricket, volleyball and buzkashi; Ghazi Stadium and other sports grounds.
profile.transportation: Kabul International Airport, buses/minibuses/taxis, Kabul–Jalalabad Road and Kabul–Kandahar Highway.
interestingFacts: High-elevation capital located in a mountain valley.
profile.shortDescription: Kabul is the national capital and largest urban centre of Afghanistan.

data.name: Kandahar
data.shortDescription: Kandahar is a major southern city with historic ties to the Durrani state.

profile.culture: Pashtun poetry and traditional music; Pashtunwali and jirga traditions.
profile.economy: Kandahar economy is focused on agriculture (notably grapes and pomegranates), trade, transport and growing industrial parks (Shorandam).
profile.tourism: Shrine of the Cloak, Kandahar Citadel/Old City heritage areas, Ahmad Shah Durrani Mausoleum, Arghandab Valley.
profile.overview: Major southern city; ancient settlement closely associated with Ahmad Shah Durrani and the Durrani state.
profile.transportation: Ahmad Shah Baba International Airport; buses/minibuses/taxis; Kandahar–Kabul Highway.
profile.majorIndustries: agriculture (fruit drying/packing), food processing, small-scale manufacturing
profile.traditionalFood: Kandahari naan, meat kebabs, rice dishes
profile.shortDescription: Kandahar is a major southern city with historic ties to the Durrani state.

data.name: Khost
data.shortDescription: Khost is a southeastern provincial centre with strong Pashtun cultural traditions.

profile.culture: Pashtunwali, jirga traditions, hospitality and local music.
profile.economy: Khost serves as a trading centre with Pakistan; notable local exports include pine nuts; regional trade and services drive the local economy.
profile.tourism: Local cultural and religious sites and mountain/valley landscapes.
profile.overview: Southeastern provincial centre important for regional trade and administration.
profile.transportation: Khost International Airport; minibuses and taxis; Khost–Gardez and regional roads.
profile.traditionalFood: Pashtun-style meat dishes, rice, naan and qorma
profile.shortDescription: Khost is a southeastern provincial centre with strong Pashtun cultural traditions.

data.name: Mazar-i-Sharif
data.shortDescription: Mazar-i-Sharif is a major northern city known for the Shrine of Hazrat Ali (Blue Mosque).

profile.culture: Nowruz, Eid and religious festivals; traditional music, poetry and crafts.
profile.economy: Mazar-i-Sharif is a northern trading hub: trade, agriculture, karakul sheep farming, small-scale oil and gas exploration.
profile.tourism: Shrine of Hazrat Ali (Blue Mosque), ancient Balkh and regional cultural sites.
profile.overview: Major northern city developed around the Shrine of Hazrat Ali with modern urban development largely in the 19th century.
profile.geography: Balkh River and regional irrigation; semi-arid continental climate.
profile.transportation: Maulana Jalaluddin Balkhi International Airport; regional/freight rail connection at Hairatan; buses/minibuses/taxis.
profile.majorIndustries: trade, agriculture, sheep farming, small energy exploration
profile.shortDescription: Mazar-i-Sharif is a major northern city known for the Shrine of Hazrat Ali (Blue Mosque).
